Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear set of questions. I pulled in Jordan (pricing/routing) and Vanessa (account lead) to make sure we cover both billing math and commercial options. High level answers up front:

1) Heartbeats: by default we meter per-request token usage; however, we have a session aggregation window (30 minutes by default) that groups small calls and heartbeats into a single billing bucket so you aren’t billed per tiny ping. In your case, 30s heartbeats will be aggregated with nearby short calls unless you request per-call isolation.

2) Slab boundary rounding: long calls are metered at actual token usage. For contexts that cross a slab (e.g., 16k -> 32k), we apply the slab pricing for the tokens in each slab and then apply the configured rounding quantum (typically 1 token for detailed metering, but per-account minimums and floor rules can cause effective rounding to the nearest 100 or configured unit).

3) KV reuse and credits: KV reuse reduces compute per-token but does not automatically generate a separate credit. We do offer pilot credits for predictable KV reuse cases and can amortize commit credits across sessions in enterprise packages.

Ben —

Attached is a concise worked example and a few sample invoice lines. Key assumptions are listed up front; I kept the math conservative so procurement can see worst-case exposure. Summary first, then the spreadsheet-style breakdown.

Assumptions:
- Short call: 25 tokens generated + 10 tokens input = 35 tokens total, 500 calls/day distributed across 10 users (50 calls/user).
- Heartbeat: 3 tokens per ping, 1 ping every 30s while session active; for aggregation we assume 1 heartbeat per short-call window when within the 30-minute session window (i.e., aggregated).
- Long call: 14k context read + 2k output = 16k total tokens for the call (sits right at the 16k slab).
- Pricing slabs (example): up to 16k priced at $0.0009/token, 16k-32k additional tokens at $0.0007/token. Account minimum: monthly minimum equivalent of 1,000,000 tokens (we can negotiate for pilot).

Worked example (daily):
1) Short calls: 500 calls * 35 tokens = 17,500 tokens/day.
2) Heartbeats: if aggregated inside session window, effectively absorbed into short-call buckets; worst-case if isolated it would be (1 ping/30s * 3600s/hr * active hours) — but aggregation reduces this by ~80% in typical traffic patterns.
3) Long calls: 10 long calls * 16,000 tokens = 160,000 tokens/day.

Daily token total (conservative): 177,500 tokens => Monthly (30 days): 5,325,000 tokens.

Billing math with slab and rounding examples:
- Long calls are split by slab only if they exceed slab size. In our example the 16k call lands exactly at the 16k slab so all charged at 16k slab price. If one long call were 18k, 16k would be at slab A price and 2k at slab B price.
- Rounding: we meter at token granularity. Rounding quanta apply at invoice line aggregation depending on the SKU: per-call metering uses 1-token precision; per-session or per-route minimums may be rounded to configured unit (e.g., 100-token rounding for legacy SKUs).
- Minimums: if your monthly true usage is < 1,000,000 tokens, the minimum will apply. For pilots, we typically create a short-term minimum waiver or a scaled minimum tied to committed spend.

Sample invoice lines (monthly):
- Usage (short calls + heartbeats): 525,000 tokens @ $0.0009 = $472.50
- Usage (long calls): 4,800,000 tokens @ blended rates (16k slab for most) = $4,320.00
- Subtotal usage = $4,792.50 -> If minimum applies (1,000,000 tokens @ $0.0009 = $900), you pay the higher of actual or minimum; in this case actual exceeds minimum.

Credits and amortization:
- KV cache amortization: we do not automatically credit KV reuse in metering, but for committed contracts we can provide a KV-efficiency credit (e.g., 5–15% effective discount) based on observed reuse metrics measured by our tracing hooks.

Next steps:
